paragraphs: Friend, here's what I see in this whole passage: the servant never treated his prayer and his work as two separate jobs. He prayed at the spring, and then he went right on doing the next thing, telling the story and giving God the credit. He says he "bowed down and worshiped the LORD" (Genesis 24:48), and later he "bowed down to the ground before the LORD" (Genesis 24:52). Two bows, and neither one was about himself.

Now look at what happens when the family hears it all. Laban and Bethuel say, "This is from the LORD" (Genesis 24:50), and they don't argue with it. The servant won't be talked into waiting, either. He says, "Do not delay me, since the LORD has made my journey a success" (Genesis 24:56). When God is clearly moving, the faithful thing is to keep up, and I'm telling you, I know how it feels when somebody holds the door open and you have to decide to walk through.

And then there's Rebekah. When they ask her, "Will you go with this man?" she answers, "I will go" (Genesis 24:58). Three words. Nobody could do that part for her, and that's the part I keep chewing on, baker. God does the leading, but you still have to say your own yes, and then Isaac, "comforted after his mother's death" (Genesis 24:67), shows us that God's yes can come with kindness inside it.
